provenance.instrument: Township of Penn (Westmoreland County) Code Chapter 190 Zoning (Ord. No. 912-2016, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 code date 2025-05-21 (breadcrumb). New Laws on 2026-11-26: Ord. No. 973-2025 (2025-10-15) is the only zoning amendment since; read in full on 2026-11-26. The others (972, 974 to 980) are an alley vacation, budget, traffic, tax, property maintenance, parks and impact fees.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 breadcrumb 'Code 2025-05-21'. Ord. No. 973-2025 (zoning amendment, 2025-10-15) is listed under New Laws, not yet in the code, and read from its PDF.
provenance.code_caution: Ord. No. 973-2025 (adopted 2025-10-15, not yet in the online code, read from the New Laws PDF) renames the Industrial Commerce (IC) district the Light Industrial and Commerce District (LICD), strikes '(11) Conversion apartments' from its permitted uses, keeps 'Single-family detached' with a new '(2-acre minimum)', and resets its dimensional standards; it also creates a Heavy Industrial (HI) district and a Mineral Processing Overlay. Attachment 2 (Zoning Use Table, 'Amended 2-21-2018 by Ord. No. 919') predates Ord. No. 955 (2022) and 973-2025 and disagrees with the text in places: it marks 'Conversions apartments' P in MDR, CC and IC and 'Single-family detached dwelling' P in CC and C in IC, while 190-403B lists no conversion apartments in MDR, Ord. No. 955 removed single-family detached from CC, and 190-406 permits it in LICD. No section says whether the table or the district text controls.
checks: A 'conversion apartment' is 'a dwelling unit created within an existing single-family dwelling in accordance with all applicable requirements of this chapter' (190-202). In the district text it is a permitted principal use only in the CC Commercial Corridor district (190-405B(11)). Ord. No. 973-2025 struck it from the former IC district, now LICD

Conflicting text, ask the Zoning Officer: the multifamily dwelling definition is 'a building containing three or more dwelling units, including conversion apartments' (190-202), so it is not settled whether one apartment added to a house (two units) is a conversion apartment or must meet multifamily rules

In CC a single-family detached dwelling is no longer a permitted use (repealed by Ord. No. 955 in 2022), so a house there is likely nonconforming. In LICD it is permitted on at least two acres (190-406C(28) as amended by Ord. No. 973-2025)

No standards section for conversion apartments was found. The district rules apply: CC lot 21,780 sq ft with public water and sewer (43,560 without either), at most four dwelling units per acre for multifamily (190-405F)
In MDR a duplex (two independent dwelling units, each with a separate entrance, the only principal building on the lot) is a permitted use on at least 2/3 acre (190-403B(6), 190-202)

RR, MDR, NC, LICD and HI do not list conversion apartments in their text. Conflicting text, ask: the Zoning Use Table (Attachment 2, 2018) marks conversion apartments permitted in MDR. The search found no other ADU text (accessory dwelling, accessory apartment, in-law, ECHO, granny, caretaker, accessory unit)

Parking: 'Single-family dwelling 2 for each unit'. 'Multiple-family dwelling 1 1/3 spaces for each unit with 2 bedrooms or less, and 2 for each unit having more than 2 bedrooms'. Fractions round up (190-623B, C)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Penn Township (Westmoreland County). Read on eCode360 (PE1662) in a browser, one print view at a time, on 2026-11-14. Code and New Laws search for 'accessory dwelling', 'accessory apartment', 'in-law', ECHO, granny, 'family dwelling', relative, caretaker, conversion, 'accessory unit', 'living quarters' and 'conversion apartment(s)' found the conversion apartment definition and the CC and IC listings. Use lists read for RR, MDR, NC, CC, IC and the MEO and DIO overlays (Article IV). Table 2 (Appendix A) was not opened. Second review, 2026-11-26: Ord. No. 973-2025 read in full from the New Laws PDF (strikeouts checked on the page images); Attachment 2 (Zoning Use Table) read; 190-102 and 190-403 read again in the chapter print view. Still open, the text does not settle: whether one apartment added to a house (two units) is a conversion apartment or a multifamily dwelling (190-202), and whether MDR permits conversion apartments (Attachment 2 says P, 190-403B omits them).

term.note: 'A dwelling unit created within an existing single-family dwelling in accordance with all applicable requirements of this chapter.'

status.note: A permitted principal use in CC only, inside an existing single-family dwelling (Ord. No. 973-2025 struck it from the former IC district). The multifamily definition also names conversion apartments, so the two-unit case is not settled.

status_outside.note: RR, MDR, NC, LICD and HI do not list conversion apartments in their use lists. The Zoning Use Table (Attachment 2, 2018) marks them permitted in MDR; the text and the table disagree there, so ask the Zoning Officer.

path.note: Listed among the permitted principal uses in CC. Conflicting text, ask: the multifamily definition counts conversion apartments among buildings of three or more units.

fallback_path.note: Outside CC a second unit in a house is not a listed use in the district text. It needs a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board. In MDR the Zoning Use Table (Attachment 2) marks conversion apartments permitted, which the district text does not; ask.

value.name: Duplex
value.conditions: A building with two independent dwelling units, each with a separate entrance, that is the only principal building on the lot. At least 2/3 acre. Front 30, side 15, rear 40 ft, residential coverage 35%.
value.note: Read as a path for an existing house converted to two units with separate entrances.

value.condition: The unit is created within an existing single-family dwelling.
Conflicting text, ask: the multifamily dwelling definition (three or more dwelling units) includes conversion apartments, so multifamily rules may apply to the converted building.
In CC a single-family detached dwelling is no longer a permitted use (Ord. No. 955, 2022), so the house is likely nonconforming. Ask how that affects a conversion.

types_not_addressed.note: An addition to create the unit is not named.

max_sqft.note: No size cap for a conversion apartment was found.

internal_uses_district_height.note: Inside the house. District principal height 75 ft in CC.

reading.value: Table 623 has no conversion apartment row. As a dwelling unit next to a single-family dwelling (2 for each unit) the lot needs 4 in all. Read as multifamily (1 1/3 for a unit of two bedrooms or less, rounded up to 2), also 4 for two small units.

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached with public water and sewer. One acre with on-lot utilities. Frontage 150 ft.

utility_rows.note: 'Minimum half an acre when connected to public water and sewer, minimum one acre with on-lot utilities.'

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached, 1/4 acre. Density at most two dwelling units per acre for single-family residences (190-403F(6)). Frontage 90 ft.
With both public water and sanitary sewerage. Frontage 100 ft (150 without).

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: Four dwelling units per acre for multifamily.

value.when: Neither public water nor public sewer

utility_rows.note: 'Uses without either public water or sanitary sewerage: 43,560 square feet (one acre).' A lot with only one of them is not settled by the text.

min_lot_sqft.note: 'Single-family detached (2-acre minimum)' (190-406C(28)). 'Service and residential uses' otherwise 21,780 sq ft with public water and sewer, 43,560 sq ft without. Frontage 100 ft for service and residential uses.

setback_front_ft.note: 75 ft if the lot or use is across from a residential district or use.

setback_side_ft.note: 50 ft when the use abuts a residential use or district.

setback_rear_ft.note: 50 ft if it abuts a residential district or use.

accessory_setback_side_ft.note: Accessory structures 20 ft from side and rear lot lines.

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: Four dwelling units per acre, unless otherwise specified.
